messages:
arya: Quick bakeoff update — ran GPTQ profiles across Llama2-70b, Mistral-7B-v0.2, and Qwen-7B. Focused on 4-bit/8-bit GPTQ configs (group sizes 128/256), act-ordering on/off. Short TL;DR + numbers below. Link to full notebook: https://redwood-internal/reports/gptq-bakeoff-1769203345

sam: Nice. Which evals did you run? MMLU, HumanEval, etc?

arya: Ran MMLU (multi-shot where applicable), TruthfulQA, HumanEval (pass@1) subset, and a custom production prompt set (500 prompts) that mirrors typical Redwood API traffic. Also logging token-level latency and VRAM peaks.

mike: Curious about deltas vs FP16 baseline. Any big regressions?

arya: Most deltas small but family-dependent. Quick numbers (GPTQ 4-bit g128 unless noted):
- Llama2-70b: MMLU -1.2% abs, TruthfulQA -2.8% (worst on reasoning/non-factual trick Qs), HumanEval pass@1 -0.9 pts, perplexity +0.6. VRAM reduction ~58%, throughput up 2.8x on p4d.
- Mistral-7B-v0.2: MMLU -0.6%, TruthfulQA -1.1%, HumanEval +0.2 (noise), perplexity +0.3. VRAM reduction ~62%, throughput up 3.4x on our A10 tests.
- Qwen-7B: MMLU -1.8%, TruthfulQA -3.5% (largest drop), HumanEval -1.0, perplexity +1.1. VRAM reduction ~60%, throughput up 3.1x.

elaine: Are these with act-ordering enabled? AWQ comparisons?

arya: Baseline GPTQ runs had act-ordering ON for Llama and Mistral. For Qwen we tried both; act-ordering helped ~0.4% on MMLU. AWQ (INT4-like) was run on a small subset: AWQ matched GPTQ on Mistral but caused larger deltas on Llama/Qwen; AWQ latency slightly better but accuracy cost higher.

devin: Did you test group size sensitivity? Any sweet spot?

arya: Yes — g128 vs g256. Llama2 improved ~0.2% going g256 but VRAM/throughput tradeoff hurts (throughput -8%). Mistral stable across group sizes. Qwen slightly better at g256 too. Conclusion: g128 is best default for hosted (throughput cheaper), offer g256 profile in Dedicated for accuracy-sensitive customers.

sam: Any catastrophic failures / hallucination regressions on the production prompt set?

arya: No catastrophic failures, but saw a 4% increase in short-form factual hallucinations on Qwen GPTQ4. We flagged 32 prompts where entailment confidence dropped; attaching a short CSV in the report.

mike: Memory/speed numbers for inference? Batch size & seq length?

arya: Bench setup: batch=1 (streaming), seq=1024 prompt+gen when noted. P4d and A10 pooled runs: median token latency reductions — Llama2: 0.35→0.13s/token, Mistral: 0.22→0.07s/token, Qwen: 0.24→0.08s/token. VRAM peaks listed per-model in report.

eval-bot: AUTO-EVAL: MMLU baseline 68.4 -> GPTQ4 67.2 (delta -1.2); HumanEval baseline 32.1 -> GPTQ4 31.2 (delta -0.9). Full table: https://redwood-internal/evals/gptq-1769203345.csv

elaine: Good to know. Recommendations for deployment?

arya: Proposal:
- Hosted API: ship GPTQ4 g128 for Mistral-7B as default (low delta, big wins).
- Hosted: offer GPTQ4 for Qwen/Mistral with a warning flag in docs for edge cases; add prompt-level QA gating for flagged categories.
- Dedicated: offer Llama2-70b GPTQ g256 as a premium accuracy profile.
- Private/on-prem: provide both GPTQ and FP16 images; recommend customer eval harness.

devin: Any tooling we need to add to Redwood Optimize/Console?

arya: Yes — add per-model quantization profile metadata to model catalog (expected delta/% tokens saved), automated eval hooks that re-run the 500-production prompts post-deploy, and an alert if hallucination rate increases >3% vs baseline.

sam: Can we add quick toggle in console to prefer accuracy vs cost so customers pick g128 vs g256 easily?

arya: Yup — I'll open a ticket for console config (DEVX-2314).

mike: Outstanding follow-ups?

arya: Next steps:
1) Run full AWQ sweep on Llama2/Qwen (scheduled tomorrow) — check INT4 viability.
2) Build prompt-level gating rules from the 32 flagged prompts (we can generalize patterns).
3) Create a small canary fleet for Mistral-GPTQ on Hosted with 5% traffic and safety hooks.

elaine: Thanks — add me to the canary plan. :+1:

arya: Will do. If anyone wants the raw logs/CSV ping me and I’ll share.

devin: Thanks for the summary — looks actionable.

arya: End of thread — full notebook in the link above, will post AWQ results after sweep.
